user_review.method: Maintainer walkthrough of user-facing routing and release instructions, plus executed temporary-repository tests of missing, stale, committed and unrelated evidence. Walkthroughs are explicitly simulated; no human study or independent review is claimed.

scenarios.request: Make my self-authored skill usable, without separately saying publish.
scenarios.expected: Complete user review, comparable research, refinement, source and standalone release under the owner standing policy.
scenarios.observed: Instruction walkthrough follows Finish the whole skill and lifecycle.md; global and registry policy supply release authority and final receipt requirements.

scenarios.request: Explore a private draft skill only.
scenarios.observed: Instruction walkthrough takes the explicit draft/private exception; a read-only audit likewise does not run the full release sequence.

scenarios.request: Publish a changed skill with no review, an old hash, or failed validation.
scenarios.expected: Reject release until current evidence and successful validation exist.
scenarios.observed: Fixture tests rejected missing, source-stale, metadata-stale and incomplete/failed evidence; committed checks also rejected a receipt that existed only locally.

scenarios.request: Publish a reviewed skill while another skill has an unrelated review draft.
scenarios.expected: Allow the reviewed target while preserving unrelated work.
scenarios.observed: Fixture test accepted the clean target; unrelated review draft stayed outside its release boundary.

similar_skills.learned: Skill quality requires behavioral scenarios and observing failure/retest, beyond Markdown or YAML validity.
similar_skills.reason: The lifecycle records normal and boundary outcomes honestly and uses executable checks for release mechanics.

similar_skills.learned: Inspect outputs against user intent and iterate on usefulness; keep detailed evaluation guidance separate from core routing.
similar_skills.reason: The compact core loads lifecycle guidance on demand and asks for evidence that outcomes helped, rather than equating a score with user value.

similar_skills.learned: A universal strict test-first or multi-agent procedure adds ceremony to every edit.
similar_skills.reason: Review depth scales to the material change, and simulated versus executed results remain explicit; trivial wording does not require a new agent team.

validation.observed: 21 tests passed, including evidence freshness, committed source boundaries, unrelated draft preservation, and discovery snapshot integrity.
Skill frontmatter and structure passed the installed authoring validator.
